Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

# Conservative Party Manifesto 2024 - Summary

## Economic Vision and Tax Cuts

The Conservative manifesto centres on economic stability following COVID-19 and the Ukraine crisis, highlighting falling inflation, rising real wages, and returning growth. The party pledges significant tax cuts, including halving employee National Insurance from 12% to 6% by April 2027 (saving average workers £1,350), abolishing self-employed National Insurance entirely, and introducing the "Triple Lock Plus" to protect pensioners from income tax on state pensions.

## Immigration and Border Security

The Conservatives promise to introduce a legally binding cap on migration that falls annually, with parliamentary votes on levels. They commit to stopping illegal Channel crossings through the Rwanda deportation scheme, reforming international asylum rules, and increasing visa fees while requiring health checks for migrants.

## Defence and National Security

Defence spending will increase to 2.5% of GDP by 2030, representing the largest sustained increase since the Cold War. Priorities include boosting UK defence manufacturing, investing £10 billion in munitions production, and maintaining support for Ukraine. The party pledges to strengthen NATO and establish new defence partnerships.

## Public Services

NHS spending will increase above inflation annually, with plans to recruit 92,000 more nurses and 28,000 more doctors. The manifesto promises 50 new Community Diagnostic Centres, expanded Pharmacy First services, and 250 new or modernised GP surgeries. Mental health support will expand to 100% of schools by 2030.

## Housing and Infrastructure

The party targets 1.6 million new homes through brownfield development, planning reforms, and abolishing EU nutrient neutrality rules. First-time buyers will benefit from permanent Stamp Duty relief up to £425,000 and a new Help to Buy scheme. Transport investment includes £36 billion from HS2 savings for local projects and extending the £2 bus fare cap.

## Young People and Education

A mandatory National Service programme will offer 18-year-olds military placements or civic volunteering. Education reforms include the Advanced British Standard for 16-19 education, 100,000 new apprenticeships funded by closing poor-quality university courses, and mobile phone bans in schools.

## Energy and Environment

The Conservatives commit to net zero by 2050 through a "pragmatic" approach, including annual North Sea oil and gas licensing, trebling offshore wind capacity, and expanding nuclear power with Small Modular Reactors. They guarantee no new green levies while protecting agricultural land from solar farms.

## Community and Rural Support

The farming budget increases by £1 billion with a legal food security target. Rural communities receive continued broadband investment and transport support. The manifesto promises neighbourhood police officers for every area and tougher action on anti-social behaviour.
